chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Rifa'a ibn Musa from Aban ibn Taghlib said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'With what should I proclaim the Talbiyah?' He said: 'Do not specify, neither Hajj nor Umrah, but intend in your heart the 'Mut'ah (Hajj al-Tamattu'), for if you catch the season of Umrah before the Hajj days, you will be a Mutamatti', and otherwise you will be a Hajj (Qarini/Hajj al-Qiran or just Hajj).

key_terms.أُهِلُّ: To proclaim the Talbiyah and enter the state of Ihram
key_terms.حَاجًّا: A Hajj (one who performs Hajj directly or as Qarini)
key_terms.لَا تُسَمِّ: Do not specify (the type of pilgrimage)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: A Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: How should one intend the Ihram for Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Aban ibn Taghlib highlights the flexibility of the Shia jurisprudence regarding the intention (niyyah) for Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the pilgrim need not explicitly declare the type of pilgrimage but rather hold the intention of 'Mut'ah' in the heart. This allows for a pragmatic approach where one enters Ihram with the hope of performing Umrah first, but retains the option to remain in the state of Hajj if circumstances prevent the completion of Umrah. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the internal state of intention over rigid verbal declaration, facilitating ease for the pilgrim.
